name: Sterling
description:
Most recliners look like medical equipment. Bulky proportions, exposed mechanisms, an undeniable sense that they were engineered for function and styled afterwards. Sterling was built the other way around — we started with the silhouette of a structured sofa, and asked our mechanical team to fit the recline mechanism inside it.

Two independent motors — one for the back, one for the footrest — operate from separate controls, so the position is yours to dial in. Structured back panels keep lumbar support exactly where it should be even after thousands of cycles. USB ports recessed into each seat charge phones from the seated position without being announced. The technology disappears; the seat remains.

Sterling tends to be the second recliner in the room — the considered upgrade after a customer has lived with a basic recliner and decided to do better.

name: Orbit
description:
A statement sofa for rooms that can hold one. The curved form does two things — it softens an otherwise rectilinear room, and it forces the seating to face inward, making conversation the natural use rather than television.

Orbit is genuinely made-to-order. Custom-curved frames are more expensive to build because we don't reuse jigs across orders — every Orbit is bent on a frame dimensioned to the buyer's room. The arc you see in the showroom is one configuration; yours can be tighter, wider, or a different chord length entirely. That's why the price is what it is.

Fabric choice matters more on Orbit than on a rectangular sofa. The curve catches light differently along its length, and patterned fabrics distort visually around the bend. Our design lead will steer you toward solid, tactile fabrics — and away from prints that fight the form.

name: Boho Nest
description:
Boho Nest is the unconventional piece in our Signature range — wooden slat construction visible through the cushions, lower seat height than typical, a designed aesthetic closer to a retreat than to a standard living room.

The cushions sit on the slats; the slats sit on a solid wood base. No upholstered apron, no skirting — the construction is the design. Pairs naturally with linen and cotton upholstery in earth palettes; less natural with velvets or formal fabrics.

Works best in homes that lean toward Japandi, organic-modern, or boho aesthetics. Looks out of place in classical or maximalist rooms.

name: Zaddy
description:
Zaddy is the contemporary sofa in our range. Where Batavia is balanced and Eclipse is plush, Zaddy is sharp — straight edges, slim arms, a tight back-cushion profile that reads architectural rather than soft.

The restraint is intentional. Zaddy is what we recommend in rooms where the sofa is one of several considered objects: where there's a designed light, a picked-by-hand rug, a piece of art on the wall. A more comfortable but more expressive sofa would compete with all of that. Zaddy doesn't compete; it sits.

The trade-off is comfort. Zaddy is firmer than our other sofas — designed for upright sitting rather than full-recline lounging. Customers who want to lie on their sofa should pick Eclipse or Batavia instead.

name: Eclipse
description:
Eclipse is the sofa we built for rooms that are doing more with less — apartments where the sofa has to be the focal piece without dominating the space, and homes where the dominant aesthetic is restraint. The defining detail is the exposed steel frame: visible, intentional, the construction itself as part of the design.

The thinking: most premium sofas sold in India are designed around hidden engineering — the frame disappears into the upholstery, the legs do the styling work. Eclipse goes the other way. The structural steel runs visibly along the underside and the legs, finished cleanly, sized to be looked at rather than hidden. It's a design decision rather than a cost decision; structural steel costs more than a hidden plywood-and-leg arrangement, but the visual outcome is something we couldn't get any other way.

Construction: minimalist steel frame in a brushed or matte finish, structural rather than decorative. The seat platform is engineered plywood over the steel substructure. Cushions sit on the platform with no upholstered apron — the cushion edge is the silhouette. 32-density foam in the seat cushions; back cushions softer. Eight stitches per inch on every visible seam. The L-shape configuration sits on extended steel runners; the corner reads as a single piece rather than two pieces joined.

Materials: full 4,000-fabric library across all four tiers. Eclipse reads particularly well in linen, cotton-linen blends, and the bouclé-textured fabrics in our Imported tier — the visible frame creates a contrast with soft, textured upholstery that flat-fabric doesn't deliver. Leather works but reads more conventional; Eclipse is a fabric piece by design intent. Cushion fill is interchangeable — softer down-feather option available at the Imported tier for the lounge-piece feel.

Configuration: three-seater straight, three-seater + lounger (the L-shape), or four-seater corner. Specify chaise side. Specify steel frame finish — brushed silver or matte black; the matte black is what we'd recommend for industrial-modern rooms, brushed silver for lighter palettes. Bring room dimensions and we'll size the corner depth to fit. The minimalist construction means Eclipse looks correct in rooms most other sofas would crowd.

Lead time 14–25 days. Limited warranty applies: seven years on structural frame, three years on foam and cushion core (two years for Super Soft foam), and one year on upholstery workmanship; extended coverage, where offered, is confirmed on the invoice. Steel frame is structurally stable past most furniture lifespans — the upholstery is what'll need refreshing first, and re-upholstery is available at cost in any of our four fabric tiers.

name: Riva
description:
Riva is the L-shape sofa that converts to a bed without compromising on either job. Most sofa-cum-beds we've seen do one job well and the other badly — comfortable as a sofa but the bed is a board, or comfortable as a bed but the sofa cushions sit oddly. Riva is dimensioned to do both jobs at the level you'd expect from a dedicated piece.

The thinking: studio apartments, guest rooms, and home offices in Bangalore are getting smaller, and the math of buying a separate sofa and a separate guest bed often doesn't work. But the Indian market for sofa-cum-beds has historically been the cheap end — futons sold under the label, or click-clack mechanisms with thin foam over plywood. We wanted to build a sofa-cum-bed that someone would actually want to sleep on — dimensioned right for an adult, with the convertible mechanism engineered to last past the warranty.

Construction: 18mm BWP plywood frame across the bed deck — the same thickness we use for our dedicated bed range, because the sofa-cum-bed has to support the same loads when in bed mode. The fold-out mechanism is heavy-gauge steel with two pivot points, sized to handle thousands of cycles without play. Foam is layered: 32-density at the base for support, 25-density medium-soft at the contact layer for sleep comfort. The cushion stack is engineered so the back cushions slot into the bed frame as the upper third of the sleeping surface — no separate mattress needed, no compromise on the sofa silhouette.

Materials: full 4,000-fabric library across all four tiers. Velvet works particularly well on Riva because the L-shape geometry catches light at multiple angles. Performance fabric is what we'd recommend for guest-room use — easier to clean if a guest stays multiple nights. Full-grain leather is also offered, though we'd note that leather on a convertible mechanism wants the right finish so it doesn't dry out at the fold lines.

Configuration: standard size sleeps two adults at queen dimensions when fully extended. Specify left-hand or right-hand chaise. Storage compartment under the chaise is optional — useful for bedding when the sofa is in everyday use. Arm style and leg finish customisable. Bring room dimensions and we'll size the corner depth to match.

Lead time 14–25 days. Seven-year structural frame warranty, three-year foam and cushion core warranty (two years for Super Soft foam), one-year upholstery workmanship warranty, and one-year warranty on the convertible mechanism.

name: Felini
description:
Felini is our flagship leather sectional — a five-seater L-shape designed around the geometry of genuine leather. Most leather sofas in the Indian market are bonded or PU dressed up to look like the real thing; Felini is offered in imported full-grain Italian leather as the primary upholstery, which behaves differently and ages differently.

The thinking: leather changes the math on a sofa. It's heavier, so the frame has to be stiffer. It catches light differently, so the cushion geometry has to be more considered — a leather cushion with the wrong stuffing reads as flat. And it ages — full-grain leather develops a patina over five to seven years that no fabric can replicate. Felini is built around that timeline. It's the sofa that looks better at year five than at year one.

Construction: hardwood frame with corner-block reinforcement at every load point. 32-density foam in the seat, slightly firmer than our fabric sofas because leather tightens the cushion read — softer foam under leather goes mushy. Bonded leatherette is offered as the entry tier; genuine Italian leather is the Imported tier and is what the piece was originally designed around. SS (stainless steel) legs as standard — the brushed metal reads cleaner against leather than wooden legs, which is why we picked it for the original spec.

Materials, the distinctives: full-grain Italian leather (Imported tier) is sourced through a Bangalore importer with traceable hide records; the leather is hand-cut to pattern in our Kudlu Gate workshop rather than machine-cut, because cutting on a hide requires reading the grain. Movable headrest at the upper back — adjustable upward for reading or relaxed viewing, dropped down to maintain the sofa silhouette. The stitch detailing is single-needle topstitch at 8 stitches per inch, contrast-piped on the Imported tier.

Configuration: 5-seater is the original spec; 6-seater and 7-seater are available. Specify left-hand or right-hand chaise. Specify leather grade — bonded, full-grain Italian, or full-grain Belgian. Specify color from our leather swatch book; standard colors include white, ivory, taupe, and chocolate, with custom dye lots possible at the Imported tier on lead-time extension.

Lead time 14–25 days. Seven-year structural frame warranty, three-year foam and cushion core warranty (two years for Super Soft foam), and one-year upholstery workmanship warranty. Re-upholstery in any of our four fabric tiers available at cost — Felini's frame outlasts most upholstery cycles, and the leather can be repolished or replaced separately.
key_features: Italian leather, five-seater, sectional. The corner sofa.

name: Edizioni
description:
Edizioni is the piece in our Signature range built for rooms where the sofa is meant to be looked at — not tucked under a bookshelf, not pushed against a wall, not making peace with the rest of the furniture. It anchors the space. It's the answer to the question "where does the room start."

The thinking: most premium sofas in India are imports — flown in from Italy or Indonesia, sized for European living rooms, sold at multiples that include three layers of margin and a six-month wait. We wanted to build something at that craftsmanship tier without the import calculus. Edizioni is what came out of that brief — a fully customisable statement sofa, made in our workshop, dimensioned to your room before a single staple goes in.

Construction: 16mm BWP-grade plywood frame, joined at every load point. 32-density minimum, varies by comfort level foam in the seat cushions; back cushions softer for body weight to settle into. Eight stitches per inch on every visible seam — slower to build, and what separates a piece that holds shape at year five from one that puckers at month eighteen. Frames are jointed and tested in our workshop before upholstery — you're welcome to see this done if you visit Kudlu Gate.

Materials, the part that matters: Edizioni is offered in our full 4,000-fabric library across four tiers — Comfort-Zone, Leatherette, Exclusive Collections, and Vegan & Genuine Leather. The Imported and Designer tiers include Italian and Belgian woven fabrics; leather is offered in PU, bonded, and full-grain genuine across all configurations. The piece reads differently in each — velvet gives it weight; linen makes it informal; full-grain leather is what most clients land on when this is going to be the only sofa in the room.

Configuration: pick three-seater, four-seater, sectional, or a curved arrangement. Pick chaise side. Pick arm style — straight or rolled. Pick legs — tapered wood, brushed brass, or hidden plinth. Specify back depth if your usual sofas feel too shallow or too cavernous. Our studios at Kudlu Gate and Millers Road show the changes with sample frames.

Lead time is 14–25 days from confirmed order. Seven-year structural frame warranty, three-year foam and cushion core warranty (two years for Super Soft foam), and one-year upholstery workmanship warranty. Re-upholstery available at cost for the life of the piece — Edizioni is built once and re-finished as the room around it changes.
key_features: A statement sofa, custom-built — the room's anchor.

name: Leha
description:
Leha is built as an L-shape — designed to anchor a corner and let traffic flow around it.

Most leather sofas in India are designed for showrooms — high-gloss, structured, slightly uncomfortable to sit on for two hours. Leha is dimensioned the other way: matte bonded leather, deeper seat than the showroom standard, stitched-back detail that softens what would otherwise be a hard line.

The imported residential-grade seat belts inside the seat are the part you don't see. They're what give a leather sofa proper sit — without them, a leather sofa is just leather over a board, and you feel the board within months. The bonded leather is easier to clean than full-grain (a real consideration in homes with kids or pets) but sits and ages similarly.

Leha works well in living rooms with darker walls or natural wood. The matte finish reads richer than glossy leather and doesn't show every fingerprint.
key_features: A leather sofa, dimensioned for living.
Frame: Premium Pine Wood + 16mm BWP plywood + Indonesian pine

name: Chesterfield
description:
A traditional Chesterfield with deep button-tufting on the back and arms, rolled arm scrolls, low-set seat profile — but in a sage upholstery rather than the conventional oxblood or chestnut. The shift in colour does something quiet: it makes the silhouette feel current without losing the heritage.

We built the Chesterfield for compact Indian living rooms, where a full-sized British original would dominate. Proportions are tighter, the seat slightly higher than the original, but construction details are unchanged — every button hand-tied through the back, every arm-scroll wrapped by hand, traditional turned beech-wood legs.

Works well in homes with traditional architectural details — high ceilings, wooden floors, picture rails. Less well in clinical-modern rooms; the form fights the room.

name: Akiva
description:
Akiva is the armchair we built for the moment when a living room is almost done but needs one more piece — the corner chair, the reading chair, the chair next to the bookcase. It's one of our Quick Ship pieces — ready in about 7 days instead of the usual 14–25, because we keep a few finished pieces in our most-ordered fabric.

The thinking: most furniture decisions in a new home come in waves. The sofa goes first, the dining table follows, the bedroom is last. By the time the room is mostly furnished, the realisation hits that there's a corner that needs a chair — not another sofa, not an ottoman, but a single seat that holds the room together. The traditional answer is to wait another month for a custom piece. Akiva is the alternative: a fully designed accent chair, available in our most popular fabric in a quick-ship configuration, ready in seven days.

Construction: structured back and arms over a solid hardwood frame. 32-density foam, eight stitches per inch on every visible seam — same construction standard as our custom range, no quality difference between the quick-ship and the made-to-order configurations. Tapered wooden legs in a choice of finishes. The silhouette is sleek enough to fit a contemporary room and structured enough to read in a more traditional one — Akiva is intentionally style-neutral so it works as the additive piece rather than competing with the dominant aesthetic.

Materials: quick-ship configurations are stocked in three or four bestselling fabrics — usually a sage velvet and a charcoal woven, refreshed seasonally. Made-to-order configurations open up the full 4,000-fabric library across all four tiers; lead time on those is 14–25 days like our other pieces. The wooden legs are solid (not veneer) in walnut, oak, or natural finish.

Configuration: standard dimensions are 31" H × 28" W × 25.5" D — sized to be a comfortable single seat, not an oversized lounge piece. Quick-ship is one configuration, one fabric option per stock cycle. Made-to-order opens up dimension changes (deeper seat, taller back, wider arms), fabric choice, and leg finish. Visit Kudlu Gate or Millers Road to sit in the standard dimensions before specifying changes.

Lead time: 7 days for quick-ship, 14–25 days for made-to-order. Seven-year structural frame warranty, three-year foam and cushion core warranty (two years for Super Soft foam), and one-year upholstery workmanship warranty.
